rows.reference: Sytrus is a six-operator FM, RM, additive, and subtractive synthesizer.
rows.aurum: Aurum is an independently identified six-operator FM, RM, additive, and filtered instrument with its own version-13 configuration.

rows.reference: Six operators can act as carriers or modulators through a freely configured modulation matrix, including self-feedback.
rows.aurum: Six fixed operators feed bipolar 6x6 FM and RM matrices with bounded one-sample feedback and independent 6x3 output routing.

rows.reference: Each operator supports custom shapes, noise, plucked synthesis, morphing, and a 128-harmonic amplitude/phase editor with sample resynthesis.
rows.aurum: Each operator offers sine, triangle, saw, square, wavefold, or a 16-harmonic amplitude-only additive editor. Harmonic phase, 128 bins, noise, plucked mode, and operator sample resynthesis are absent.

rows.reference: Operator articulation uses multi-segment envelopes, LFOs, and mappings across pitch, volume, pan, velocity, random, unison, and other targets.
rows.aurum: Each operator has amplitude, pitch, and phase ADSRs plus five-point velocity/key gain curves, and shared sources can drive its level or pan. Multi-segment envelopes, tuning modulation, dedicated per-operator LFOs, and random/unison maps are absent.

rows.reference: Separate FM and RM behavior supports bipolar amounts, feedback, carrier output assignment, and operator/filter/effect routing.
rows.aurum: Separate bipolar FM and RM matrices, self-feedback, phase-inverted sends, and live graph diagnostics render and persist in browser/native paths.

rows.reference: Three state-variable filter modules support broad routing and filter articulation.
rows.aurum: Two output filters provide low-pass, band-pass, or high-pass modes with cutoff, resonance, drive, serial/parallel routing, and shared-source cutoff modulation. A third filter and resonance/drive articulation are absent.

rows.reference: Operators can feed three filters, effects, panned dry output, and the final mix from the matrix.
rows.aurum: A bipolar 6x3 matrix sends each operator to Filter A, Filter B, or Direct, with per-operator pan before the buses and shared Beat instrument/track routing afterward.

rows.reference: Unison exposes order, pan, volume, pitch, sub-level, phase, envelope variation, and programmable per-property mapping.
rows.aurum: Aurum exposes one-to-eight voices, detune, and stereo spread. Volume, sub-level, phase, envelope variation, and property mapping are absent.

rows.reference: Global volume/pitch/envelope offsets, mono-key behavior, and X/Y performance controllers shape the patch.
rows.aurum: Mono, legato, glide, voice limit, operator velocity/key response, and editable pitch-bend range are present. X/Y controllers and global envelope offsets are absent.

rows.reference: Extensive envelopes, LFOs, velocity, keyboard, random, and performance mappings can target operator/filter parameters.
rows.aurum: Schema v13 reuses Beat's shared route IDs and evaluator for Envelope 1, tempo-synced LFO 1, two independently editable macros, velocity, keytrack, mod wheel, or pressure. Destinations are bounded to master level/pan, six operator level/pan pairs, and Filter A/B cutoff, resonance, and drive, with visible local summaries and browser/native/persistence tests. Additional sources and tuning/matrix targets remain absent.

rows.reference: Many operator and articulation controls can be automated or driven by note/performance mappings, subject to Sytrus matrix limitations.
rows.aurum: Pitch bend is rendered and telemetry-tested; native pressure, velocity, keytrack, and mod-wheel routes evaluate per voice. Browser audition captures the current expression snapshot, and verified precedence makes direct automation replace manual destinations, macro automation replace persisted macro sources, and expression routes remain additive. Continuous mid-audition browser expression still needs a streaming preview path.

rows.reference: A patch includes a three-band EQ, chorus, three serial/parallel delay lines, reverb, and effect sends.
rows.aurum: Aurum enters Beat's ordered instrument FX, track FX, and send/return graph, but has no Aurum-native EQ/effect routing page matching the Sytrus patch workflow.

rows.reference: Operator settings can be copied/pasted and the matrix supports rapid routing experimentation.
rows.aurum: Initialize, copy, paste, swap, reset, seven algorithm templates, signal diagnostics, keyboard tab navigation, and bounded transactional undo/redo are present and verifier-covered.

rows.reference: Sytrus provides a mature preset ecosystem and patch workflow.
rows.aurum: Versioned Aurum records share Beat's generic browser with user save/delete, immutable factory sounds, name/tag search, separate per-user favorites, metadata-driven audition, identity-safe apply, migration, and malformed/future rejection. Beat-authored Factory Bank v2 covers seven production families with zero-neutral v13 performance routes and bounded render metrics; human listening sign-off remains open.

rows.reference: Complex operator, unison, filter, and effect configurations trade CPU for depth.
rows.aurum: Selectable 1x/2x/4x network quality, dense feedback stability, exact work telemetry, and two bounded realtime load tiers are verified. Release-machine limits and broader supported-load tiers remain open.

rows.reference: Reference behavior must be measured locally before any sound or CPU parity claim.
rows.aurum: Native live/export parity is verified at 44.1, 48, and 96 kHz. Browser/native bounded-difference, alias-energy, perceptual cross-rate, accessibility, and listening gates remain open.
